text: 鎌倉幕府（かまくらばくふ）は、源頼朝が創設した日本の武家政権。
en: The Kamakura shogunate TOP, [is] the samurai government of Japan that Minamoto no Yoritomo founded.
romaji: kamakurabakufu ( kamakurabakufu ) wa, minamotonoyoritomo ga sousetsu shita nippon no buke seiken.

text: この時代を鎌倉時代という。
en: This era ACC [one] calls the Kamakura period.
romaji: kono jidai o kamakurajidai toiu.

text: 頼朝の死後、幕府に仕えた坂東武士（御家人）の権力闘争によって、頼朝の嫡流（源氏将軍）は断絶し、将軍職は藤原氏からの摂家将軍、さらに皇族出身の宮将軍へと継承された。
en: After Yoritomo's death, through the power struggle of the Bando warriors (gokenin) who served the shogunate, Yoritomo's main line (the Genji shoguns) died out, and the shogunal office was passed on to regent-house shoguns from the Fujiwara and further to princely shoguns of imperial birth.
romaji: yoritomo no shigo, bakufu ni tsukae ta bandou bushi ( o kajin ) no kenryoku tousou niyotte, yoritomo no chakuryuu ( genji shougun ) wa danzetsu shi, shougun shoku wa fujiwara shi karano sekke shougun, sarani kouzoku shusshin no miya shougun heto keishou sareta.

text: しかしこの過程で将軍は名目上の存在となり、北条氏による執権、やがて北条義時の嫡流である得宗、末期はその陪臣（御内人）である内管領が鎌倉幕府の実質的な支配者となった。
en: But in this process the shogun became a nominal existence, and the regency by the Hojo clan, then the tokuso, the main line of Hojo Yoshitoki, and in the final period the uchi-kanrei, who were its rear vassals (miuchibito), became the de facto rulers of the Kamakura shogunate.
romaji: shikashikono katei de shougun wa meimokujou no sonzai tonari, houjoushi niyoru shikken, yagate houjou yoshitoki no chakuryuu dearu tokusou, makki hasono baishin ( o uchibito ) dearu nai kanryou ga kamakurabakufu no jisshitsuteki na shihaisha tonatta.

text: 元弘3年（1333年）閏2月に船上山で後醍醐天皇が挙兵すると、幕府は名越高家と足利尊氏を鎌倉方の総大将として派遣するが、同年4月27日に高家が戦死し、4月29日に高氏が反幕府側に寝返ると、5月8日に関東で新田義貞が寝返って鎌倉に攻め入り、短期間のうちに形勢が変わり、同年5月22日に鎌倉幕府は滅亡した。
en: When in the 2nd intercalary month of Genko 3 (1333) Emperor Go-Daigo raised an army at Mt. Senjo, the shogunate dispatches Nagoe Takaie and Ashikaga Takauji as commanders-in-chief of the Kamakura side, but on the 27th of the 4th month of the same year Takaie fell in battle, and when on the 29th Takauji went over to the anti-shogunate side, on the 8th of the 5th month Nitta Yoshisada in the Kanto went over and attacked into Kamakura, within a short time the situation changed, and on the 22nd of the 5th month of the same year the Kamakura shogunate perished.
romaji: genkou 3 nen ( 1333 nen ) uruu 2 gatsu ni senjou yama de godaigo tennou ga kyohei suruto, bakufu wa nagoya kouke to ashikaga takauji o kamakura hou no soudai shou toshite haken suruga, dounen 4 gatsu 27 nichi ni kouke ga senshi shi, 4 gatsu 29 nichi ni takauji ga hanbaku fu gawa ni negaeru to, 5 gatsu 8 nichi ni kantou de nitta yoshisada ga ne kaetsu te kamakura ni seme iri, tankikan nouchini keisei ga kawari, dounen 5 gatsu 22 nichi ni kamakurabakufu wa metsubou shita.

text: 鎌倉幕府が築いた武家政権の基礎は、室町幕府および江戸幕府へと継承された。
en: The foundation of samurai government that the Kamakura shogunate built was passed on to the Muromachi shogunate and the Edo shogunate.
romaji: kamakurabakufu ga kizui ta buke seiken no kiso wa, muromachibakufu oyobi edobakufu heto keishou sareta.

text: 『吾妻鏡』によれば、治承4年（1180年）12月12日に鎌倉の大倉郷に頼朝の邸となる大倉御所が置かれ、また幕府の統治機構の原型ともいうべき侍所が設置されて武家政権の実態が形成された。
en: According to the Azuma Kagami, on the 12th day of the 12th month of Jisho 4 (1180) the Okura palace, which became Yoritomo's residence, was placed in Okura village of Kamakura, and the samurai-dokoro, which one might call the prototype of the shogunate's governing structure, was established, and the substance of a samurai government was formed.
romaji: ( azuma kagami ) niyoreba, jishou 4 nen ( 1180 nen ) 12 gatsu 12 nichi ni kamakura no ookura sato ni yoritomo no tei tonaru ookura gosho ga oka re, mata bakufu no touchi kikou no genkei tomoiubeki samuraidokoro ga setchi sarete buke seiken no jittai ga keisei sareta.

text: 朝廷は寿永二年十月宣旨（1183年）で頼朝に対し、東国における荘園・公領からの官物・年貢納入を保証させると同時に、頼朝による東国支配権を公認した。
en: The court, by the Juei 2 tenth-month edict (1183), made [someone] guarantee to Yoritomo the delivery of official goods and annual tribute from estates and public lands in the eastern provinces, and at the same time officially recognized Yoritomo's right to rule the east.
romaji: choutei wa juei ninen juugatsu senji ( 1183 nen ) de yoritomo ni taishi, toukoku niokeru shouen ・ kouryou karano kanmotsu ・ nengu nounyuu o hoshou saseruto doujini, yoritomo niyoru toukoku shihaiken o kounin shita.

text: 壇ノ浦の戦い（元暦2年/寿永4年（1185年））で平氏を滅ぼし、同年、文治の勅許（文治元年（1185年））では頼朝へ与えられた諸国への守護・地頭職の設置・任免を許可した。
en: [∅] destroyed the Taira at the battle of Dan-no-ura (Genryaku 2 / Juei 4 (1185)), and in the same year, by the Bunji imperial sanction (Bunji 1 (1185)), [the court] permitted the establishment and appointment/dismissal of shugo and jito posts in the provinces granted to Yoritomo.
romaji: dannoura no tatakai ( genryaku 2 nen / juei 4 nen ( 1185 nen ) ) de heishi o horobo shi, dounen, bunji no chokkyo ( bunji gannen ( 1185 nen ) ) deha yoritomo e atae rareta shokoku heno shugo ・ jitou shoku no setchi ・ ninmen o kyoka shita.

text: そして建久元年（1190年）頼朝が権大納言兼右近衛大将に任じられ、公卿に列し荘園領主の家政機関たる公文所（のちの政所）開設の権を得たことで、いわば統治機構としての合法性を帯びるようになり、建久3年（1192年）には征夷大将軍の宣下がなされた。
en: And in Kenkyu 1 (1190), because Yoritomo was appointed acting Grand Counsellor and Right Commander of the Inner Palace Guard, joined the kugyo, and obtained the right to open a kumonjo (later mandokoro), the household office of estate proprietors, [it] came to carry, so to speak, legitimacy as a governing structure, and in Kenkyu 3 (1192) the proclamation [of appointment] as seii taishogun was made.
romaji: soshite kenkyuu gannen ( 1190 nen ) yoritomo ga ken dainagon kanemigi konoe taishou ni nin jirare, kugyou ni retsu shi shouen ryoushu no kasei kikan taru kumon tokoro ( nochino mandokoro ) kaisetsu no ken o eta kotode, iwaba touchi kikou toshiteno gouhousei o obi ruyouninari, kenkyuu 3 nen ( 1192 nen ) niha seii daishougun no senge ganasareta.

text: こうして、名実ともに武家政権として成立することとなった。
en: In this way, it came to be that [it] was established, in name and substance, as a samurai government.
romaji: koushite, meijitsu tomoni buke seiken toshite seiritsu surukototonatta.

text: 守護の設置で幕府は諸国の治安維持を担当したものの、当初は特に西日本では朝廷およびその出先機関である国府、寺院との三重支配状態だったが、次第に範囲を拡大。
en: Although by setting up the shugo the shogunate took charge of keeping order in the provinces, at first, particularly in western Japan, [it] was in a state of triple rule with the court and its outpost organs, the kokufu, and the temples, but gradually expansion of the range.
romaji: shugo no setchi de bakufu wa shokoku no chian'iji o tantou shitamonono, tousho wa tokuni nishinihon deha choutei oyobisono desaki kikan dearu kou, jiin tono mie shihai joutai dattaga, shidai ni han'i o kakudai.

text: 光合成（こうごうせい、ひかり-、英語: photosynthesis）とは、光エネルギーを化学エネルギーに変換して生体に必要な有機物質を作り出す反応過程をいう。
en: Photosynthesis TOP-QUOT, [one] calls [it] the reaction process that converts light energy into chemical energy and produces the organic substances necessary for living bodies.
romaji: kougousei ( kougousei, hikari -, eigo : photosynthesis ) toha, hikari enerugii o kagaku enerugii ni henkan shite seitai ni hitsuyou na yuukibutsu shitsu o tsukuridasu hannou katei woiu.

text: 葉緑体を持つ一部の真核生物（緑色植物、植物プランクトン、藻類）や、原核生物であるシアノバクテリアが行う例がよく知られている。
en: Examples that some eukaryotes having chloroplasts (green plants, phytoplankton, algae) and cyanobacteria, which are prokaryotes, perform are well known.
romaji: youryoku karada o motsu ichibu no shinkaku seibutsu ( ryokushoku shokubutsu, shokubutsu purankuton, sourui ) ya, genkaku seibutsu dearu shianobakuteria ga okonau rei gayoku shira reteiru.

text: これらの光合成生物（photosynthetic organism）は、光から得たエネルギーを使って、二酸化炭素からグルコースのような炭水化物を合成する。
en: These photosynthetic organisms, using energy obtained from light, synthesize carbohydrates like glucose from carbon dioxide.
romaji: korerano kougousei seibutsu ( photosynthetic organism ) wa, hikari kara eta enerugii o tsukatte, nisankatanso kara gurukoosu noyouna tansuikabutsu o gousei suru.

text: この合成過程は炭素固定と呼ばれ、生命の体を構成するさまざまな生体物質を生み出すために必須である。
en: This synthesis process is called carbon fixation, and is indispensable in order to produce the various biological substances that make up the body of life.
romaji: kono gousei katei wa tanso kotei to yoba re, seimei no karada o kousei surusamazamana seitai busshitsu o umidasu tameni hissu dearu.

text: また、生物圏における物質循環に重要な役割を果たしている。
en: Also, [it] is playing an important role in material cycling in the biosphere.
romaji: mata, seibutsuken niokeru busshitsu junkan ni juuyouna yakuwari o hata shiteiru.

text: 光合成は、狭義では光エネルギーを利用した炭素固定反応のみを指すが、広義では光エネルギーを利用した代謝反応全般を指す。
en: Photosynthesis, in the narrow sense, refers only to the carbon fixation reaction that uses light energy, but in the broad sense refers to metabolic reactions in general that use light energy.
romaji: kougousei wa, kyougi deha hikari enerugii o riyou shita tanso kotei hannou nomiwo sasu ga, kougi deha hikari enerugii o riyou shita taisha hannou zenpan o sasu.

text: 光エネルギーを利用する生物は一般に光栄養生物（phototroph）と呼ばれ、光エネルギーを利用して二酸化炭素を固定する光独立栄養生物（photoautotroph）と、光からエネルギーは得るものの、炭素源として二酸化炭素ではなく有機化合物を用いる光従属栄養生物（photoheterotroph）に分かれる。
en: Organisms that use light energy are generally called phototrophs, and divide into photoautotrophs, which use light energy to fix carbon dioxide, and photoheterotrophs, which though they get energy from light, use organic compounds rather than carbon dioxide as carbon source.
romaji: hikari enerugii o riyou suru seibutsu wa ippanni kouei youjou mono ( phototroph ) to yoba re, hikari enerugii o riyou shite nisankatanso o kotei suru hikari dokuritsu eiyou seibutsu ( photoautotroph ) to, hikari kara enerugii wa eru monono, tanso gen toshite nisankatanso dehanaku yuukikagoubutsu o mochii ru hikari juuzoku eiyou seibutsu ( photoheterotroph ) ni waka reru.

text: 狭義では光独立栄養生物のみを光合成生物とするのに対して、広義では光栄養生物と光合成生物は同義となる。
en: Whereas in the narrow sense [one] takes only photoautotrophs as photosynthetic organisms, in the broad sense phototrophs and photosynthetic organisms become synonymous.
romaji: kyougi deha hikari dokuritsu eiyou seibutsu nomiwo kougousei seibutsu tosurunoni taishi te, kougi deha kouei youjou mono to kougousei seibutsu wa dougi tonaru.

text: 多くの光合成生物は炭素固定に還元的ペントース・リン酸回路（カルビン回路）を用いるが、それ以外の回路も存在する。
en: Many photosynthetic organisms use the reductive pentose phosphate cycle (Calvin cycle) for carbon fixation, but other cycles also exist.
romaji: ooku no kougousei seibutsu wa tanso kotei ni kangen teki pentoosu・rin san kairo ( karubin kairo ) o mochii ruga, sore igai no kairo mo sonzai suru.

text: 光合成は、反応過程で酸素分子を発生するか否かで、酸素発生型（oxygenic）および酸素非発生型（anoxygenic）の大きく2種類に分けられる。
en: Photosynthesis is divided, by whether or not [it] generates molecular oxygen in the reaction process, broadly into 2 kinds, oxygenic and anoxygenic.
romaji: kougousei wa, hannou katei de sanso bunshi o hassei suruka inaka de, sanso hassei kata ( oxygenic ) oyobi sanso hi hassei kata ( anoxygenic ) no ookiku 2 shurui ni wake rareru.

text: 酸素発生型および酸素非発生型の光合成システムは互いに一部相同で進化的に関連しており、現在の地球上で支配的なのは、植物やシアノバクテリアが行う酸素発生型光合成である。
en: Oxygenic and anoxygenic photosynthetic systems are partly homologous to each other and evolutionarily related, and what is dominant on the present earth is the oxygenic photosynthesis that plants and cyanobacteria perform.
romaji: sanso hassei kata oyobi sanso hi hassei kata no kougousei shisutemu wa tagaini ichibu soudou de shinkateki ni kanrenshi teori, genzai no chikyuujou de shihaiteki nanoha, shokubutsu ya shianobakuteria ga okonau sanso hassei kata kougousei dearu.

text: 酸素発生型の光合成の普及に伴い、本来酸素のほとんど存在しなかった地球上に酸素分子が高濃度で蓄積するようになり、現在の地球環境が形作られた。
en: Accompanying the spread of oxygenic photosynthesis, molecular oxygen came to accumulate at high concentration on an earth where originally almost no oxygen existed, and the present earth environment was shaped.
romaji: sanso hassei kata no kougousei no fukyuu ni tomonai, honrai sanso nohotondo sonzai shinakatta chikyuujou ni sanso bunshi ga kounoudo de chikuseki suruyouninari, genzai no chikyuukankyou ga katazukura reta.

text: 消費税（しょうひぜい、（英: consumption tax）は、商品の販売やサービスの提供などの取引に対して課される租税である。
en: Consumption tax (shohizei, (Eng.: consumption tax) TOP, is a tax levied on transactions such as the sale of goods and the provision of services.
romaji: shouhizei ( shouhizei, ( ei : consumption tax ) wa, shouhin no hanbai ya saabisu no teikyou nadono torihiki ni taishi te kasa reru sozei dearu.

text: 日本における消費税は消費一般に広く課税する間接税であり、一般に付加価値税と呼ばれるものの一形態（消費型付加価値税（仕入控除方式））である。
en: Consumption tax in Japan is an indirect tax that taxes consumption in general broadly, and is one form of what is generally called value-added tax (consumption-type VAT (input-credit method)).
romaji: nippon niokeru shouhizei wa shouhi ippanni hiroku kazei suru kansetsuzei deari, ippanni fukakachi zei to yoba rerumonono ichikeitai ( shouhi katatsuki ka kachi zei ( shiire koujo houshiki ) ) dearu.

text: 本来の消費税という用語はさらに広い概念を指す。
en: The original term consumption tax refers to a still broader concept.
romaji: honrai no shouhizei toiu yougo hasarani hiroi gainen o sasu.

text: 付加価値税はフランスで1959年に初めて導入され、その後160カ国以上で導入された。
en: Value-added tax was first introduced in France in 1959, and thereafter was introduced in more than 160 countries.
romaji: fukakachi zei wa furansu de 1959 nen ni hajimete dounyuu sare, sono nochi 160 ka kuni ijou de dounyuu sareta.

text: OECD加盟国で付加価値税を導入していないのは、州ごとに税制が大きく異なり、売上税（sales Tax）と物品税（excise tax）が導入されているアメリカ合衆国のみである。
en: What has not introduced VAT among OECD member states is only the United States, where tax systems differ greatly by state and sales tax and excise tax are introduced.
romaji: OECD kameikoku de fukakachi zei o dounyuu shiteinainoha, shuu gotoni zeisei ga ookiku kotona ri, uriage zei ( sales Tax ) to buppinzei ( excise tax ) ga dounyuu sareteiru amerika gasshuukoku nomidearu.

text: 州税と地方税の合計である売上税の税率は各州の市ごとに0%-10%と異なっている。
en: The rate of sales tax, which is the sum of state tax and local tax, differs city by city of each state, 0%-10%.
romaji: shuuzei to chihouzei no goukei dearu uriage zei no zeiritsu wa kakushuu no shi gotoni 0%-10% to kotona tteiru.

text: 日本では1989年の消費税法制定で導入された。
en: In Japan [it] was introduced with the enactment of the Consumption Tax Act of 1989.
romaji: nippon deha 1989 nen no shouhizei housei tei de dounyuu sareta.

text: 事業者が事業として対価を得て行う資産の譲渡、資産の貸付け及び役務の提供、商品の販売や運送、広告など、対価を得て行う国内の取引のほとんどは課税の対象となり、外国から製品を輸入する場合も課税される。
en: Most domestic transactions done for consideration, such as transfer of assets, lending of assets and provision of services, sale and transport of goods, advertising, which businesses do as business receiving consideration, become objects of taxation, and the case of importing products from abroad is also taxed.
romaji: jigyousha ga jigyou toshite taika o ete okonau shisan no jouto, shisan no kashitsuke ke oyobi ekimu no teikyou, shouhin no hanbai ya unsou, koukoku nado, taika o ete okonau kokunai no torihiki nohotondoha kazei no taishou tonari, gaikoku kara seihin o yunyuu suru baai mo kazei sareru.

text: 2012年時点でOECD諸国の平均では付加価値税は税収の約31%を占めており、これはGDPの6.6%に相当する。
en: As of 2012, on the OECD average, VAT accounts for about 31% of tax revenue, and this corresponds to 6.6% of GDP.
romaji: 2012 nenji ten de OECD shokoku no heikin deha fukakachi zei wa zeishuu no yaku 31% o shime teori, koreha GDP no 6. 6% ni soutou suru.

text: EUでは、加盟国には付加価値税の導入と共に標準税率を15%以上にすることが義務付けられている。
en: In the EU, member states are obligated, together with introducing VAT, to make the standard rate 15% or more.
romaji: EU deha, kameikoku niha fukakachi zei no dounyuu to tomoni hyoujunzeiritsu o 15% ijou nisurukotoga gimuzuke rareteiru.

text: 租税体系からの分類方法の一つとして、所得課税（所得税、法人税）、資産課税（相続税、固定資産税）、そして消費課税に大別する方法がある。
en: As one of the classification methods from the tax system, there is a method of roughly dividing into income taxation (income tax, corporate tax), asset taxation (inheritance tax, fixed-asset tax), and consumption taxation.
romaji: sozei taikei karano bunruihouhou no hitotsu toshite, shotoku kazei ( shotokuzei, houjinzei ), shisankazei ( souzokuzei, koteishisanzei ), soshite shouhi kazei ni taibetsu suru houhou gaaru.

text: この消費課税はさらに、消費した本人へ直接的に課税する直接消費税と、消費行為を行なったものが担税者であるものの、納税義務者ではない間接消費税に分類できる。
en: This consumption taxation can further be classified into direct consumption tax, which taxes the consuming person directly, and indirect consumption tax, where the one who performed the act of consumption is the tax bearer but not the taxpayer.
romaji: kono shouhi kazei hasarani, shouhi shita honnin e chokusetsuteki ni kazei suru chokusetsu shouhizei to, shouhi koui o okona ttamonoga tanzei mono dearumonono, nouzei gimu mono dehanai kansetsu shouhizei ni bunrui dekiru.

text: 夏目 漱石（なつめ そうせき、1867年2月9日〈慶応3年正月5日〉 - 1916年〈大正5年〉12月9日）は、日本の明治末期から大正初期にかけて活躍した小説家・俳人、英文学者、教育者。
en: Natsume Soseki (1867-02-09 - 1916-12-09) TOP, [is] a novelist/haiku poet, English literature scholar, educator of Japan who was active from the late Meiji to the early Taisho period.
romaji: natsume souseki ( natsume souseki, 1867 nen 2 gatsu 9 nichi < keiou 3 nen shougatsu 5 nichi > - 1916 nen < taishou 5 nen > 12 gatsu 9 nichi ) wa, nippon no meiji makki kara taishou shoki nikakete katsuyaku shita shousetsuka ・ haijin, eibungaku mono, kyouikusha.

text: 武蔵国江戸牛込馬場下横町（現：東京都新宿区喜久井町）出身。
en: From Babashita-yokocho, Ushigome, Edo, Musashi province (now Kikuicho, Shinjuku, Tokyo).
romaji: musashi kuni edo ushigome baba shita yokochou ( gen : toukyoutoshinjukuku yoshihisa imachi ) shusshin.

text: 本名は夏目 金之助（なつめ きんのすけ）。
en: Real name TOP Natsume Kinnosuke.
romaji: honmyou wa natsume kinnosuke ( natsume kinnosuke ).

text: 俳号は愚陀仏。
en: Haiku name TOP Gudabutsu.
romaji: haigou wa gu dabutsu.

text: 日本の近現代文学史を代表する文豪の一人と評価されている。
en: [He] is evaluated as one of the literary giants representing the history of modern Japanese literature.
romaji: nippon no kingendai bungaku shi o daihyou suru bungou no hitori to hyouka sareteiru.

text: 代表作は、『吾輩は猫である』『坊っちゃん』『三四郎』『それから』『こゝろ』『明暗』など。
en: Representative works TOP, 'I Am a Cat', 'Botchan', 'Sanshiro', 'And Then', 'Kokoro', 'Light and Darkness', etc.
romaji: daihyousaku wa, ( wagahai wa neko dearu ) ( botchan ) ( sanshirou ) ( sorekara ) ( ko ゝ ro ) ( meian ) nado.

text: 講演録に『私の個人主義』がある。
en: Among lecture records there is 'My Individualism'.
romaji: kouen roku ni ( watashi no kojinshugi ) gaaru.

text: 作品を通して、今日に通用する言文一致の現代書き言葉の確立に寄与した。
en: Through [his] works [he] contributed to the establishment of the modern written language of genbun-itchi that is valid today.
romaji: sakuhin o toushi te, kyou ni tsuuyou suru genbun'itchi no gendai kakikotoba no kakuritsu ni kiyo shita.

text: 帝国大学（のちの東京帝国大学、東京大学）英文科卒業後、松山で愛媛県尋常中学校教師、熊本で第五高等学校（熊本大学の前身）教授などを務め、文部省留学生としてイギリスへ留学して大ロンドンのカムデン区、ランベス区などに居住した。
en: After graduating from the English department of the Imperial University (later Tokyo Imperial University, University of Tokyo), [he] served as teacher at Ehime Prefectural Ordinary Middle School in Matsuyama, professor at the Fifth Higher School (predecessor of Kumamoto University) in Kumamoto, etc., went to study in Britain as a Ministry of Education overseas student, and lived in Camden, Lambeth, etc. of Greater London.
romaji: teikoku daigaku ( nochino toukyou teikoku daigaku, toukyoudaigaku ) eibunka sotsugyougo, matsuyama de ehimeken jinjou chuugakkou kyoushi, kumamoto de daigo koutougakkou ( kumamotodaigaku no zenshin ) kyouju nadowo tsutome, monbushou ryuugakusei toshite igirisu e ryuugaku shite dai rondon no kamuden ku, ranbesu ku nadoni kyojuu shita.

text: 帰国後は東京帝国大学講師として英文学を講じ、講義録には『文学論』がある。
en: After returning [he] lectured on English literature as lecturer at Tokyo Imperial University, and among lecture records there is 'Theory of Literature'.
romaji: kikokugo wa toukyou teikoku daigaku koushi toshite eibungaku o kouji, kougiroku niha ( bungakuron ) gaaru.

text: 明治の文豪として、1984年（昭和59年）に発行開始された日本の千円紙幣の肖像に採用された。
en: As a literary giant of Meiji, [he] was adopted for the portrait of Japan's thousand-yen note, whose issue started in 1984 (Showa 59).
romaji: meiji no bungou toshite, 1984 nen ( shouwa 59 nen ) ni hakkou kaishi sareta nippon no sen'en shihei no shouzou ni saiyou sareta.

text: 慶応3年正月（西暦1867年2月）、夏目金之助は幕末の江戸にて、名主の夏目小兵衛直克・千枝夫妻の末子（五男）として出生した。
en: In the first month of Keio 3 (Feb. 1867), Natsume Kinnosuke was born in Edo of the late shogunate as the youngest child (fifth son) of the village headman Natsume Kohei Naokatsu and his wife Chie.
romaji: keiou 3 nen shougatsu ( seireki 1867 nen 2 gatsu ), natsume kinnosuke wa bakumatsu no edo nite, nanushi no natsume kohee naokatsu ・ chie fusai no masshi ( itsuo ) toshite shusshou shita.

text: 茶道（さどう/ちゃどう）は、湯を沸かし、茶を練（ね）るか点（た）てる、あるいは淹れ、茶を振る舞う日本伝統の行為（茶の儀式）。
en: Sado TOP, [is] a traditional Japanese act (tea ceremony) of boiling water, kneading or whisking tea, or else steeping it, and serving tea.
romaji: sadou ( sadou / chadou ) wa, yu o waka shi, cha o ren ( ne ) ruka ten ( ta ) teru, aruiha en re, cha o furu mau nihondentou no koui ( cha no gishiki ).

text: また、それを基本とした様式と芸道。
en: Also, the style and the art-way based on it.
romaji: mata, sorewo kihon toshita youshiki to geidou.

text: 主客の一体感を旨とし、茶碗に始まる茶道具や茶室の床の間にかける禅語などの掛け物は個々の美術品である以上に全体を構成する要素として一体となり、茶事として進行するその時間自体が総合芸術とされる。
en: Taking as principle the sense of unity of host and guest, the tea utensils beginning with the tea bowl and the hanging scrolls such as Zen phrases hung in the tokonoma of the tea room, more than being individual art objects, become one as elements composing a whole, and that very time proceeding as a chaji is regarded as a total art.
romaji: shukaku no ittaikan o mune toshi, chawan ni hajima ru chadougu ya chashitsu no tokonoma nikakeru zengo nadono kake mono wa kokono bijutsuhin dearu ijou ni zentai o kousei suru youso toshite ittai tonari, chaji toshite shinkou surusono jikan jitai ga sougou geijutsu tosareru.

text: 現在一般に、茶道といえば抹茶を用いる茶道のことだが、江戸期に成立した煎茶を用いる煎茶道も含む。
en: Currently, generally, if [one] says sado [it] is the sado that uses matcha, but [it] also includes senchado, which uses sencha and was established in the Edo period.
romaji: genzai ippanni, sadou toieba matcha o mochii ru sadou nokotodaga, edoki ni seiritsu shita sencha o mochii ru sencha michi mo fukumu.

text: 元来「茶湯（さのゆ、ちゃのゆ）」といった。
en: Originally [it] was called 'chanoyu'.
romaji: ganrai ( chanoyu ( sanoyu, chanoyu ) ) toitta.

text: 千利休は「数寄道」、古田織部は「茶湯」と呼んでいたが、小堀遠州は「茶の道」と呼んで「道」の字が使われ始め、やがて江戸時代17世紀後半には茶道（さどう）とも呼ばれるようになった（『茶話指月集』『南方録』など）。
en: Sen no Rikyu called [it] 'sukido', Furuta Oribe 'chanoyu', but Kobori Enshu called [it] 'cha no michi' and the character 'do' started to be used, and eventually in the late 17th century of the Edo period [it] came to be called also sado.
romaji: sen rikyuu wa ( suki michi ), furuta oribe wa ( chanoyu ) to yon deitaga, kobori enshuu wa ( cha no michi ) to yon de ( michi ) no jiga tsukawa re hajime, yagate edojidai 17 seikikouhan niha sadou ( sadou ) tomo yoba reruyouninatta ( ( sawa shigetsu shuu ) ( nanpou roku ) nado ).

text: 表千家や千家以外の多くの流派では「さどう」、裏千家では「ちゃどう」と読む。
en: In Omotesenke and many schools other than the Senke [it] is read 'sado', in Urasenke 'chado'.
romaji: omote senke ya senke igai no ooku no ryuuha deha ( sadou ), urasenke deha ( chadou ) to yomu.

text: 「茶道」の英語訳としては tea ceremony (ティーセレモニー) のほか、茶道の表千家と裏千家ではそれぞれ the way of tea(ザ ウェイ オブ ティー)、chanoyu を用いている。
en: As English translations of 'sado', besides tea ceremony, Omotesenke and Urasenke of sado use 'the way of tea' and 'chanoyu' respectively.
romaji: ( sadou ) no eigoyaku toshiteha tea ceremony ( teiiseremonii ) nohoka, sadou no omote senke to urasenke dehasorezore the way of tea( za uei obu teii ), chanoyu o mochiite iru.

text: 岡倉覚三（天心）は英文の著書 The Book of Tea（『茶の本』）において、Teaism と tea ceremony という用語を使い分けている。
en: Okakura Kakuzo (Tenshin), in his English book The Book of Tea, distinguishes the terms Teaism and tea ceremony.
romaji: okakura kakuzou ( tenshin ) wa eibun no chosho The Book of Tea ( ( cha no hon ) ) nioite, Teaism to tea ceremony toiu yougo o tsukaiwake teiru.

text: 茶道で用いる抹茶は用いる湯の量により濃茶（こいちゃ）と薄茶（うすちゃ）に分かれる。
en: The matcha used in sado divides, by the amount of hot water used, into koicha and usucha.
romaji: sadou de mochii ru matcha wa mochii ru yu no ryou niyori koicha ( koicha ) to usucha ( usucha ) ni waka reru.

text: 濃茶を作ることを「濃茶を練る（ねる）」、薄茶を作ることを「薄茶を点てる（たてる）」という。
en: Making koicha [one] calls 'kneading koicha', making usucha 'whisking usucha'.
romaji: koicha o tsukuru kotowo ( koicha o neru ( neru ) ), usucha o tsukuru kotowo ( usucha o ten teru ( tateru ) ) toiu.

text: 千利休の時代には「お茶といえば濃茶を指し、薄茶の時のみ、特に薄茶または後の薄茶と記述されて」おり、現在の茶道でも、濃茶を「主」、薄茶を「副（そえ）」、「略式」と捉えている。
en: In Sen no Rikyu's era, 'if [one] said tea [it] referred to koicha, and only in the case of usucha [it] was written specially as usucha or later usucha', and in present sado too, [one] regards koicha as 'main' and usucha as 'secondary (soe)', 'abbreviated form'.
romaji: sen rikyuu no jidai niha ( o cha toieba koicha o sashi, usucha no tokino mi, tokuni usucha mataha nochino usucha to kijutsu sarete ) ori, genzai no sadou demo, koicha o ( shu ), usucha o ( fuku ( soe ) ), ( ryakushiki ) to torae teiru.
